summary: sitecard exposes workspace SSH gateway through public tunnel with unauthenticated default
details: sitecard is a documented remote-development tool that issues temporary SSH access to a workspace. When the operator runs `sitecard start`/`serve`, the package launches an AsyncSSH gateway on 127.0.0.1 and bridges it to the public internet via a user-selected tunnel provider (srv.us by default; upterm, cloudflare, cloudflared, devtunnel are also wired up). The default CLI mode is `--public-access`/`--accept`, which allows shell and SFTP from any party who obtains the public tunnel URL with no handshake authentication; a `--no-public-access` mode enabling key/password auth is available. The capability is openly disclosed in the README and PKG-INFO ("Fresh Sitecard sessions allow public access by default because they are disposable"). The channel is not started by any install or import hook — it requires an explicit foreground CLI subcommand. The package does not read ~/.aws, ~/.ssh host keys, ~/.npmrc, browser or messaging stores, does not scrape process environment, and does not exfiltrate workspace contents to any author-controlled destination; the only outbound control plane is the operator-chosen tunnel provider. The combination of a world-reachable shell via public tunnel with no default authentication is an insecure default (CWE-306 missing authentication) in an otherwise disclosed remote-dev product.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
